name: Layered plastic frame
summary: A spectacle frame cut and polished from sheets of celluloid or acetate, often two or more layers of colour glued together before cutting.
how: Press the layers of plastic into one sheet, 3 to 5 mm thick.
Cut the front and the temples with a saw or a router, then tumble and polish them.
Warm the front and bend it to the curve of the face; fit the hinges with rivets.

origin.note: Celluloid starts to replace horn and tortoiseshell in spectacle frames; it is cheap, it polishes and it takes a tortoiseshell pattern.

adoptions.via: The browline frame joins a heavy plastic bar to a thin metal rim, and the cat-eye layers colours on the upper edge.
